messages:
maya: Quick heads up — kicking off a targeted canary for Driver 535.86 + FW 2.14 on a small GPU pool in us-west-2. Objective: measure Xid frequency and ECC deltas vs baseline (last 7d). Starting 10 cards, 6h smoke window, then expand if green. Ping @paul for gating queries and @samir for drain ops.

paul: ack. can you paste the exact queries + thresholds you want? also do we have capacity to replace any blown cards without hitting spot limits? :thinking_face:

maya: putting the queries here. primary gating: Xid per-card-rate drop >= 40% and no increase in ECC corrected/unrecoverable rate. Use these two: 

```
// XID spike rate per GPU (1h rolling)
metrics
| where name == "gpu_xid_count"
| summarize rate_per_hour = (max(value) - min(value))/1 by gpu_id, bin(timestamp, 1h)
| where rate_per_hour > 0
```

```
// ECC corrected/unrec per GPU (24h aggregated)
metrics
| where name in ("gpu_ecc_corrected", "gpu_ecc_unrecoverable")
| summarize total = sum(value) by gpu_id, name
```

maya: thresholds we care about: Xid rate <= baseline * 0.6 OR absolute <= 0.05 xids/hr (whichever larger). ECC_unrecoverable must not increase by >10% relative to baseline.

samir: for drain plan — prefer rolling replace for any card that spikes during canary. If replacement rate exceeds 2 cards/hour consider pausing and escalating. We have 5 spare cards in us-west-2 pool, but spot capacity could be tight around EOD PST.

jen: how are we differentiating driver vs kernel interactions? last time some nodes only got stable after kernel micropatch. Are we testing kernel combos?

maya: good call. canary matrix includes two kernel families: 5.15.0-70 (current prod) and 5.15.0-76 (candidate). We'll run driver+fw with both kernels across the 10 cards (5 each) to surface regressions. Keep a note: if Xid drops only on the new kernel, that's a kernel->driver interaction.

paul: added a composite alert query to SLO dashboard to show canary vs prod window side-by-side. I'll share dashboard link in a minute. Also added a synthetic workload (llama-smoke, seq=512 tokens) to reproduce KV cache churn.

infra-bot: deploy-started: canary job 2054326789 started by maya on pool us-west-2-small-c. Tags: driver=535.86, fw=2.14, kernel=5.15.0-70/76.

maya: experiment notes: 1) enable per-request KV cache telemetry (sampling=1/20) for these cards 2) enable kernel oops capture and automatic stacktrace upload to S3 prefix `s3://redwood-infra/canaries/2054326789/` 3) keep logs for 72h.

lia: during last run we saw thermal throttling correlate with Xid bursts. Are we capturing power draw/VRAM temps at 30s granularity?

maya: yes — telemetry pipeline set to 30s for temps/power only for canary cards.

samir: operational playbook if Xid bursts > 3x baseline on a single card within 30m: 1) isolate VM, 2) repro workload on spare host, 3) attempt driver hot-reload (`sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia`), 4) if still reproduces, rotate card and mark suspect for RMA. If hot-reload reduces Xid by >50% we keep card in rotation and schedule deeper burn.

paul: small addition — have an automated check to compare driver build ID and module symbol versions. Sometimes ABI mismatches cause subtle memory corruption. Query: `modinfo nvidia | grep -E "^version|^srcversion"`

jen: cost note — if we rotate cards during working hours we may trigger spot replenishment that spikes spend. Samir, can we schedule replacements for low-cost window (02:00-06:00 UTC)?

samir: yes. replace window set to 03:00 UTC by default unless it's a critical capacity event. I'll also set a throttle: max 1 rotate per 30m unless escalation tag set.

maya: fallback plan if canary shows mixed signals: 1) rollback driver on canary cards to previous stable (534.21) and run a 12h extended smoke 2) if rollback doesn't restore baseline, pause rollout and open incident for deeper kernel/firmware correlation 3) if rollback restores baseline, mark 535.86 candidate with flag `requires-kernel-76` and continue phased rollout with kernel pinning.

paul: dashboard shared: https://console.redwood.tech/dashboards/infra/canary/2054326789 (contains side-by-side Xid/ECC/thermal/power panels + per-card traces).

infra-bot: canary-step: analyze-complete for step=smoke_window. Results: xids_avg_drop=47%, ecc_unrec_delta=+2%, thermal_delta=+0.8C. Further expansion approved by gating rules.

maya: expansion plan — increase to 30 cards across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 (to test region variance) with same kernel splits. Keep replace throttle.

lia: quick sanity — eu-west has different PSU model; we'll tag telemetry and include PSU vendor in data so we can correlate hardware vendor interactions.

samir: after expansion we'll run 24h burn and then compare 7d windows. If any region shows regression we stop expansion for that region only.

paul: FYI I added a new alert that triggers if any single card exceeds baseline xids by 250% and the hot-reload fails twice within 1h — that will page oncall.

jen: thanks team. after expansion let's reconvene and decide on fleetwide rollout cadence + any kernel pinning policy. :thumbsup:

maya: agreed. I'll post a short postmortem-style note with final numbers and recommended next steps once the 24h runs complete.

infra-bot: deploy-finished: canary job 2054326789 expansion started at 2054326808.
